NVIDIA 2Q Revenue Surges 106% YoY; FY2028 Revenue Expected to Grow 70% NVIDIA announced its fiscal 2Q27 results on August 26, reporting record revenue of $96.22 billion, up 106% YoY. Data Center revenue reached $89.02B, surging 117% YoY and serving as the company’s primary growth engine. Looking ahead, NVIDIA expects third-quarter revenue to reach approximately $108B. CFO Colette Kress said during the earnings call that FY2028 revenue is expected to grow by around 70%, with the outlook constrained primarily by supply chain capacity rather than a lack of market demand.  Vera Rubin Platform Enters Full Production Commenting on current market developments, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang said AI has reached an inflection point, with the technology now capable of performing useful work and generating productive, economically valuable tokens. He emphasized that the global AI infrastructure buildout is advancing at full speed, while NVIDIA’s latest Vera Rubin platform has entered full-scale production. Huang added that companies will eventually operate multiple AI agents on a continuous basis, potentially driving a 15- to 100-fold increase in overall computing requirements.  Gross Margins Face Downward Pressure Despite maintaining a strong gross margin of 75% in the second quarter, NVIDIA is expected to face mounting cost pressures. Kress noted that surging AI demand has tightened memory supply, with extreme pricing conditions exceeding the company’s previous expectations and likely to persist through next year. NVIDIA has therefore lowered its gross margin outlook. The company expects gross margin to decline to 74% in the third quarter and bottom out at 71–72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72–73% in the first quarter of FY2028.  Huang Addresses Circular Financing Concerns NVIDIA’s substantial investments in frontier AI labs have raised market concerns over so-called “circular financing.” Kress acknowledged these concerns but said NVIDIA views these labs as once-in-a-century companies, with limited investment risk and attractive potential returns. AI labs requiring balance-sheet support are expected to account for approximately one-quarter of NVIDIA’s business next year. Huang added that NVIDIA provides a complete AI factory platform that is fundamentally different from custom inference chips designed for individual functions. He expressed confidence in NVIDIA’s technology and expects these AI labs to remain significant long-term users of the company’s computing architecture.  📊More semiconductor insights: https://buff.ly/YckK6fp 📊More financial charts: https://buff.ly/3AHP9WB
